story_text:
## The Vector Gear: More Games, Less Gambles
The Vector Gear is a headset built for creators, gamers, and enthusiasts who want to truly own their hardware. Stream, emulate and play your favorite games from a single VR/MR headset with a custom spatial OS.
We aim to turn this from a cool prototype to a polished product without any long or hard setup, similar to buying any other headset on the market. The difference?
You own the hardware you buy. We want to make technology feel more like the early 2000's, when it was more human centric.
Note: This will NOT be 3D Printed by the final product! We are going to use plastic mold injection to handle the creation of the shells for the headset! The printing you see is as these are prototypes and we do rapid prototyping.
(Feel free to visit vectorgear.xyz !)
## What It Is
When you buy a Vector Gear, you don't just get a headset. You get every way to play, more presence than any headset at this price, and the freedom to own, mod, and repair what's yours.
## The Specs
The Vector Gear features a dual 2160x2160 @ 90hz setup with automatic IPD adjustment. Additionally, each headset has full face tracking and requires no external hardware for environment tracking.
Underneath sits a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8cx Gen 3 with 8GB of RAM, paired with a dedicated RK3588s co-processor with its own 8GB, handling SLAM and face tracking. This is powered by an 85Wh silicon battery system through our connection with Amprius.
## Compute Architecture
- Qualcomm Snapdragon 8cx Gen 3 SoC (8GB RAM)
- Secondary RK3588S co-processor for tracking, sensor fusion, and developer-accessible compute tasks (8GB RAM)
- 500GB / 1TB NVMe SSD storage options
- Custom Cartridge Software Support Planned
## Display & Optics
- 2160 × 2160 per eye @ 90Hz, TFT LCD
- Pseudo-pancake optical system (Dual Combined Fresnel)
- Foveated rendering support for performance scaling planned
- Auto IPD adjustment
## Tracking & Sensing
- Inside-out SLAM tracking (headset + controllers + gloves)
- 2× monochrome SLAM cameras
- 2× interior eye tracking cameras
- 1x Interior mouth tracking camera
- 2× color passthrough cameras (global shutter)
- Full face tracking system
## Input Systems
- Steam Frame Inspired controllers
- M-DAS Glove System WIP
## Audio & Interaction
- Dual microphone array
- Audio system
## Battery & Power
- 85Wh high-density silicon battery + USB-C PD Charge
- USB-C PD charging
## Software Stack
- YuukOS (Arch-based XR distribution)
- XRUIOS spatial computing layer
- Console emulation support (iiSU partnership under discussion)
- FEX x86 emulation layer
- Proton compatibility layer
- Shinra Meisin Face Tracking (Built inhouse)
- AstroSLAM Inside Out Tracking (Built Inhouse)
## Connectivity
- Optional low-latency Wi-Fi 6E PC streaming adapter (planned)
- Wireless PCVR streaming support
## Community Friendly
At the core of the Vector Gear is a simple belief — people should own the products they buy.
That's why we make our hardware and software either source-available or fully open source. Upon release, we plan to progressively open the ecosystem — starting with more software, then hardware documentation, and eventually down to the lens design itself.
Most parts are also available for individual purchase, and you're free to use them commercially. You’re free to mod, break open, modify and do anything else you want to do with your headset!
## The Andromeda
## The Prodigal Son
When you buy an Andromeda, you get the same open ecosystem and modding freedom as the Vector Gear — purpose-built for wireless PCVR at a price that doesn't hurt.
- PCVR Focused, Wireless Foveated Streaming Planned with RK3588S Core
- Inside Out Headset + Controllers + Face Tracking
- 2160×2160 LCD or 2560x2560 OLED (per eye, although like the BSB1 @ 75hz or 1920x1920 upscaled @ 90hz)
- Auto IPD Adjustment
- Open + moddable
- 85w Amprius Silicon Battery WIP (6+ Hour Lifetime)
- Same expansion ecosystem as the Vector Gear
## Our Controllers
Both headsets come with the same controller. With upgrades on the way, the final version will feature
- Inside Out Tracking with the RK3576
- A Steam Frame Controller Based Layout
- Capacitive Tracking and
- Silicon Battery Based Power
## Built Inhouse
At Walker Industries, we take a lot of pride in most of what we do having been built inhouse! Here's a bit more behind the scenes:
## The Shinra Meisin - Face Tracker
This is a custom face tracking system we've created for eyes and mouth specifically! It currently works through OSC to feed eye and mouth data to social applications like VRChat, allowing for more expressive interactions!
We are currently working on making the cameras work with a POV from the headset through a 60 person data collection event!
## AstroSLAM - Inside Out Tracking
AstroSLAM is an inside out tracking algorithm built for the Vector Gear! It uses several state of the art techniques (such as an attention system) to offer high quality tracking to the headset and controllers alike.
Moreover, it already has a SteamVR driver!
## The XRUIOS - Spatial Computing Platform
Imagine you took the customization of Gmod and fused it with a high performance spatial runtime, giving you the power to spawn, script, and rewrite how your entire operating system while wearing it.
Just like Garry's Mod let you edit your system on the fly, the XRUIOS treats the entire spatial environment as a moddable sandbox. Turn your interface into a grimoire you use exclusively through spoken spells or a y2k callback with retro terminals! You can mix and match these to your want!
Moreover, the Continuity system within (Yuuko Protocol) allows you to continue applications from your headset to your computer and vice versa!
Also check out https://xruios.xyz!
## Where Your Money Goes/What’s Left
As a small collective of RESC (researchers, engineers, scientists and creatives), our biggest hurdle comes from the financial cost of making this all real. Most of what you see has been created on a bare minimal budget of a college student's day job, financial aid returns and competition winnings.
At first this was good, but we have reached the point where working is going to become significantly harder without finance help! Some things we want to do includes;
1. Running a large, paid event where people of all nationality types help make the face tracking as robust as possible (Monolids, skin tones, etc.)
2. Getting our motherboards quality verified by a company for both actual function and safety
3. Creating more prototypes and making manufacturing easier/cheaper
4. Paying the amazing people of Prominence for their hard work
5. Upfront costs for manufacturing (we want to make this a proper commercial headset, not something you have to put together if you don't want to)
## What it does NOT go to
1. Executive Salaries: We don’t have executives or venture capital investors breathing down our necks and we plan to stay a private company. No one is getting a bloated corporate paycheck or a fancy office off your backing.
2. Fancy Marketing Agencies: We aren't spending thousands of dollars on slick, over produced media to get a point across; everything you see is ran by us!
3. Building Digital Walls: We aren't spending a dime on DRM, proprietary lock ins, or anti repair software blocks. When you buy a Vector Gear, it's YOURS.
## Stretch Goals and Financial Honesty On Rewards
As you can tell, we weren't able to give much on discounts. Without huge angel investment firms behind us willing to take the brunt of a first batch or anything similar, we are basically running extremely lean. The 8% we lose from Kickstarter essentially means that if we were to put the discounts we wanted, we wouldn't have enough to manufacture and ship.
We hope that by creating more technology like this and with the success of this campaign, we can in the future create headsets that are overall better while also having a lower cost.
## Stretch Goals
$150k — We're Funded!
We're moving toward production! This gets us closer to turning Vector Gear from a prototype into a headset you can actually buy, set up, and use.
$200k — XRUIOS Unleashed
More customization, more spatial apps, and more ways to turn your headset into your own personal computer. We'll accelerate handheld support and begin exploring Android support, too.
$250k — M-DAS Gloves Return
We're bringing our glove based input system back into active development! More natural hand interaction, new possibilities for VR games, and another way to interact with XRUIOS beyond controllers.
$275k — Hapticore
Remember the Hapticore? It's our modular board concept for making it easier to build custom haptic controllers. We'll revisit development and work toward giving makers a more accessible way to experiment with tactile feedback and custom input hardware.
$300k — Modder Program
Early access for developers and hardware tinkerers to experiment with Vector Gear, test new ideas, and help shape the ecosystem. We want to see what people can do when they have room to build.
$350k — WalkerWorks
An accelerated early release of WalkerWorks, our store concept for indie software and hardware. We want a place where smaller developers and makers can get their projects in front of people.
$400k — Echoes Online
Development updates and a planned closed alpha for backers. We want you there while the world takes shape.
$500k — More Games, Less Gambles
More resources for software compatibility, emulation, and getting more of your favorite applications and games running on Vector Gear. Fewer walls between you and what you want to play.
$600k — GravityXR Glasses
We originally planned to release wide FOV mixed reality glasses with GravityXR with the XRUIOS within. At this milestone, we'll revisit the project and begin exploring development again alongside Vector Gear. The goal is to bring XRUIOS to a lighter form factor beyond the headset.
$750k — The Walker Industries Modding Showcase
We want to see what you build. This milestone will support a community showcase for custom interfaces, mods, accessories, and experimental hardware, with featured projects and developer spotlights.
$1M — The Next Generation
More R&D toward our next generation of hardware. We'll begin evaluating new designs, improvements, and ways to make future Walker Industries devices more capable without pricing people out.
We'll share progress as these projects develop. Manufacturing quality and getting rewards into backers' hands come first.

risks: The biggest risk comes from the development of the PCBs. While we are good enough to handle current and future additions to the software (such as creating the foveated rendering under a custom library), a mistake with the PCBs specifically would mean the headset doesn't turn on. To solve this, we are in part using the money to work with a company that's worked with the chips before specifically to QC and fix our designs.

## The Lower End Andromeda Is Now 2160x2160 @ 90hz!
Thanks to some new supplier deals and changes to our bill of materials, every Andromeda LCD now ships with 2160×2160 displays at 90 Hz. That’s the same panel resolution as the Vector Gear, at the same $650 price.
We also upgraded the battery!
In short, $650 now gets you
- 2160×2160 LCD per eye at 90 Hz (up from 1600×1600)
- Eye and mouth tracking built in
- Inside out tracking.
- Inside out tracked controllers in the box
- Wireless PCVR on a 85 Wh silicon battery pack (Upgraded from 45)

updates.title: Thank You For Your Support!
updates.text:
Hello everyone, WalkerDev here!
First and foremost, thank you to everyone who's donated over the last 24 hours! While some might connect VR crowdfunders to usually doing huge amounts in the first two days, we don't have the budget of them!
The fact that there are 12 of you who went out of your way to support a project ran by an indie group means a lot to me.
Plenty of updates coming along in the upcoming weeks!
